question: Does reconstruction-oriented assistance improve delayed unaided transfer relative to answer delegation and reference-based practice?
baseline: Direct answer delegation and ordinary documentation/practice
learner_locus: One human researcher in the initial exploratory pilot
retention_boundary: Human performance after assistance withdrawal; acquisition artifacts and AI are unavailable during assessment; the same editor/compiler/test interface remains available

dataset.holdout: Separate immediate and seven-day transfer items, hidden from learner and assistant during acquisition

protocol.stopping_rule: Twelve acquisition sessions plus their scheduled assessments; no efficacy-based stopping. Record missed sessions, attrition, extra practice, and capped or incomplete assessments.
freeze_required: randomized family-to-condition assignment within matched blocks
assistant version and complete intervention/exposure history

notes: Plan only; no human sessions scheduled or performed. Single-person results do not establish population effects, hysteresis, cognitive decline, or consciousness. Machine-learning retention requires a separate learner/state boundary and protocol.
